title: Setting up the machine for the heart

items.question: When is the cardiac screening examination optimally performed?
options: Between 18 and 22 weeks
Between 11 and 14 weeks
Between 24 and 28 weeks
After 32 weeks
items.explanation: The screening examination is performed optimally between 18 and 22 weeks.

items.question: Compared with a screen at 18 to 20 weeks, a screen at 20 to 22 weeks is:
options: Less likely to need an additional scan to complete it
More likely to need an additional scan to complete it
Not recommended
Only possible with colour Doppler
items.explanation: Screening at 20 to 22 weeks is less likely to need an additional scan for completion than at 18 to 20 weeks.

items.question: Which transducer frequency should be used for the cardiac screen?
options: The highest possible, accepting the trade-off between resolution and penetration
The lowest possible, to maximise penetration
Always the same frequency as for biometry
Frequency does not affect the cardiac image
items.explanation: The highest possible frequency should be used, accepting the trade-off between resolution and penetration.

items.question: Which group of settings does the guideline recommend for the cardiac image?
options: High frame rate, low persistence, a single focal zone, a relatively narrow field
Low frame rate, high persistence, several focal zones, a wide field
High frame rate, high persistence, several focal zones, a wide field
Low frame rate, low persistence, a single focal zone, a wide field
items.explanation: Settings should emphasise a high frame rate with increased contrast and resolution, using low persistence, a single focal zone and a relatively narrow field.

items.question: How large should the heart be on the screen?
options: At least one third to one half of the screen
About one tenth of the screen
As small as possible, to keep the whole fetus in view
Size on the screen does not matter
items.explanation: Magnify until the heart fills at least one third to one half of the screen.

items.question: When does tissue harmonic imaging help most?
options: With increased abdominal wall thickness and in the third trimester
Only in the first trimester
Only when colour Doppler is on
It reduces image quality and should be switched off
items.explanation: Harmonic imaging improves images, especially with increased abdominal wall thickness and in the third trimester.

items.question: What is cine-loop used for during the cardiac screen?
options: To assist real-time evaluation, such as confirming valve leaflet movement through the cycle
To measure the thermal index
To replace storing clips
To increase the frame rate
items.explanation: Cine-loop assists real-time evaluation, for example confirming movement of valve leaflets through the cardiac cycle.

items.question: The fetus is lying so that the outflow tracts cannot be shown. What does the guideline say may be needed?
options: Extra examination time or a second examination
Reporting the outflow tracts as normal
Leaving the outflow tracts out of the screen
Immediate referral for fetal echocardiography in every case
items.explanation: When fetal lie is unfavourable, extra examination time or a second examination may be needed.

items.question: What frame rate does the echocardiography guideline recommend for scanning the fetal heart?
options: Above 30 to 40 Hz
About 10 Hz
About 15 to 20 Hz
Frame rate is not specified
items.explanation: Frame rates above 30 to 40 Hz are recommended; a narrow sector and appropriate depth help to achieve them.
